objectives: Students should use cumulative frequency graphs to determine how many data values fall below or above certain thresholds (Maths 6.1)
Students should interpret cumulative frequency graphs to compare distributions (Maths 6.1)
Students should estimate the median, quartiles, and interquartile range from cumulative frequency graphs (Maths 6.1)

keyConcepts.explanation: A running total of frequencies which shows the number of data points below a particular value.
The median is the value below which 50% of data lies; quartiles divide data into four equal parts and can be estimated using cumulative frequency graphs.
The difference between the upper quartile (Q3) and the lower quartile (Q1), showing the spread of the middle 50% of data.

steps.title: Introduction to Cumulative Frequency Graphs
steps.content: A cumulative frequency graph helps us understand data by showing the total number of observations below a certain value. It is useful for finding medians, quartiles, and making comparisons between data sets.

steps.title: Multiple Choice Question: Interpreting the Graph
steps.content: If a cumulative frequency graph shows 40 data points below the value 50, what does this tell us?

questions.question: What does the cumulative frequency represent at value 50?
options: The total number of data points
The number of data points below 50
The number of data points above 50
The maximum value in the data
questions.answer: The number of data points below 50
questions.explanation: Cumulative frequency at a value gives the total count of observations less than or equal to that value.

steps.title: Practice Question: Using a Cumulative Frequency Graph
steps.content: A cumulative frequency graph for the scores of 60 students is shown. Use the graph to estimate:

questions.question: Approximately how many students scored less than 40?
questions.explanation: At score 40, the cumulative frequency is about 25, showing 25 students scored below 40.

questions.question: Estimate the median score.
questions.explanation: The median corresponds to half of 60, which is 30 cumulative frequency; at cumulative frequency 30, the score is about 50.

questions.question: Find the interquartile range (IQR).
questions.explanation: The lower quartile (Q1) at 15 students is around 40, and the upper quartile (Q3) at 45 students is around 60, so IQR = 60 - 40 = 20.
